[Javaagent] Rejecting every bridge removes existing controller telemetry when the implementation is inherited from an uninstrumented superclass. For example, an annotated resource interface declares `Object get()`, an unannotated superclass supplies `public String get()`, and the resource subclass extends that superclass and implements the interface. javac declares only the forwarding `Object get()` bridge on the subclass. The superclass does not match the annotation instrumentation's type matcher, so excluding the bridge leaves interface dispatch without a controller span. The same problem affects accessibility bridges on public `@Path` resources inheriting an `@GET` method from a package-private superclass without `@Path`. Preserve bridges that are the only instrumentation point, while avoiding duplicate spans for same-class covariant implementations. Add installed-agent regression coverage for both inherited cases.

Related to https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/issues/20103

Fix missing optional controller spans when JAX-RS dispatches an HTTP request to a method that narrows an inherited return type, including generic resource interfaces.

```java
interface ItemsResource<T> {
  @GET
  @Path("/current")
  T get();
}

@Path("/items")
public class ItemsResourceImpl implements ItemsResource<String> {
  @Override
  public String get() {
    return "item";
  }
}
```

With `otel.instrumentation.common.controller-telemetry.enabled=true`, `GET /items/current` now produces an `ItemsResourceImpl.get` controller span. Jersey and RESTEasy already supply `http.route` through their framework-specific instrumentation; the regression is the missing controller span, not missing route metadata in those frameworks.

The fix covers interface and superclass declarations in JAX-RS 1/2/3 and JAX-WS. Methods with different parameter types remain separate, and compiler-generated bridge methods do not produce duplicate instrumentation.

Related to #20103.
